I study how carbon, nutrients and contaminants move through soils, sediments and water. Most projects begin with a measurement problem — a sensor that drifts, a storm that arrives between samples, a core that mixes two seasons — and end with a method someone else can repeat.

Before Northfield I worked on catchment biogeochemistry in Bristol and Uppsala. The group here combines field campaigns, long-term sensors and laboratory work; the common thread is a preference for data with a visible history.
